hunks.old_text: | WC-10 | **Liveness during long waits.** The worker sends a heartbeat every 5 minutes while working. No single tool call a command makes may block the session for 4 minutes or more: a poll wait or a long eval is split into waits under 4 minutes so the session can heartbeat between them (one 300 s call is therefore not allowed). An Agent-tool subagent call, which WC-7 keeps, can also block the session, and whether a dispatched worker keeps heartbeating through a subagent call longer than 5 minutes is UNVERIFIED: the repo itself treats it as unproven until a recorded smoke check shows it (`~/.claude/commands/sc/spec-panel-ledger.md:261`). AC-0.4 records it. Until a recorded run shows heartbeats continue through such a call, the coordinator does not treat a heartbeat gap during a worker's subagent fan-out as a hang by itself; it judges liveness by `worker-list`'s `projection.liveness` and by `worker-show` (`CAPS:123`, 7.2 step 2). hunks.new_text: | WC-10 | **Liveness during long waits.** The worker sends a heartbeat every 5 minutes while working. No single tool call a command makes may block the session for longer than 240 s (4 minutes): a poll wait or a long eval is split into waits of at most 240 s so the session can heartbeat between them (one 300 s call is therefore not allowed). This is the one limit behind the cli-eval row's "waits of at most 4 minutes" and AC-4.3's "no single tool call exceeds 240 s": a call of exactly 240 s is allowed, a longer one is not (R23). An Agent-tool subagent call, which WC-7 keeps, can also block the session, and whether a dispatched worker keeps heartbeating through a subagent call longer than 5 minutes is UNVERIFIED: the repo itself treats it as unproven until a recorded smoke check shows it (`~/.claude/commands/sc/spec-panel-ledger.md:261`). AC-0.4 records it. Until a recorded run shows heartbeats continue through such a call, the coordinator does not treat a heartbeat gap during a worker's subagent fan-out as a hang by itself. `worker-list`'s `projection.liveness` and `worker-show` do not by themselves prove progress: the guide describes process liveness, and a live terminal can still hold a stuck agent (`CAPS:122-123`). Whether the fleet verdict detects a stuck but running subagent is UNVERIFIED, so the rule cannot rely on that detection. The bound is a time budget instead: the brief states the Task's longest expected run time (one more item of the section 2.3 list). The coordinator stops waiting early only on Orca's positive proof of a stall (`exited` liveness, the worker's own observed process exit, or a transcript whose final agent turn sent no `worker_done`, `CAPS:126`). When the budget passes with neither `worker_done` nor such proof, it reads the transcript with `worker-read` and escalates to the person; it never stops, retries or releases the worker on that absence alone (`CAPS:125`). Each 7.2 step-3 wait uses the smaller of its 900000 ms polling timeout and the time left in that budget; at expiry the live check fails and the coordinator escalates while preserving the Dispatch, rather than waiting forever or treating the expiry as proof of a hang (R24). (R11) | Command (wait size); worker (heartbeat); coordinator (liveness) | Cadence is from the dispatch preamble, not a guide (`CAPS:130`); pr-submit's 600 s is a cumulative per-wait budget made of repeated iterations (one foreground poll, then a sleep of at least `--poll-interval`), not one blocking call (`cmd/pr-submit.md:49`; `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:46-64`); `sk/sc-cli-eval-protocol/SKILL.md:151-152` (eval timeouts up to 3600 s) via `INV-A:65` |
